text.p: Shares in Spanish banking group Argentaria soared on Wednesday, recovering from a period of underperformance after the bank said it would reduce staff dramatically at its BEX unit, dealers said.
At 1200 GMT, Argentaria was up 270 pesetas, 3.86 percent, to 7,000 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 0.03 percent to 6,045.09.
Argentaria was benefitting from a process of stock-picking generally taking place, coming into the limelight because many other key shares are now overpriced, dealers said.

"The (Argentaria) rise is a little exaggerated, and I think this is more a reflection of the fact investors are now looking for value in terms of shares which haven't kept up with the market," said a dealer at a Spanish bank.

He added that plans to restructure the banking group were announced last year, and that details provided yesterday of staff cuts at Banco Exterior (BEX) did not really add anything to what is already known to be going on at the bank.
"It's good in that the staff cuts show what the scale of the restructuring is likely to be, but it doesn't really merit this reaction," he said.

"More than anything it shows you that really people are looking for excuses for certain stocks to go higher because in reality, all the good news is more than factored in at these (bourse) prices. I'd expect Argentaria to fall back from these levels," he added.
He expected the stock to correct, but not "substantially".
A Central Hispano Bolsa trader agreed.
"Argentaria is of the few banks that had room to rise, because all the others are now very expensive," she said.
Argentaria said on Tuesday it would cut BEX staff by 2,100 over three years, aiming to make the unit more competitive.
